# Print order APIs and identical deck version control — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Print order APIs and identical deck version control. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-11-06 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Structure and components

- [statement] DriveThruCards specifies one PDF per deck with alternating backs and faces, beginning with the first card back. PDF page order determines printed deck order, so file sequencing is part of revision control and proof review. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) — https://help.drivethrupartners.com/hc/en-us/articles/12780748203543-Specifications-for-Print-Cards
- [statement] The Game Crafter recommends inspecting one physical copy for errors and omissions before ordering multiple copies; its game definition should contain the components for one copy, with repeat copies specified by cart quantity. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-12-22) — https://help.thegamecrafter.com/article/429-how-to-order-your-game
- [statement] PrintNinja warns that a physical game proof can contain digitally printed components and that those components are not color accurate; physical proof approval must therefore distinguish which components represent production color. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-28) — https://printninja.com/proofing-options/
- [statement] Recommended release control: archive the approved artwork and component manifest under a fixed revision, record its supplier project and order identifiers, and review any reorder edits before submission. This is a workflow inference from mutable project/reorder controls and order-time freezing, not a claim that suppliers provide cryptographic artwork versioning. (medium confidence) — https://www.thegamecrafter.com/developer/Game.html · keywords: Print order APIs and identical deck version control · also: https://www.makeplayingcards.com/faq-order.aspx, https://help.thegamecrafter.com/article/110-will-my-order-include-changes-i-made-after-placing-the-order

## How it works

- [statement] The Game Crafter keeps a stable game ID while allowing updates and an edition label. Inference: neither a stable game ID nor an edition label alone demonstrates immutable artwork; the documented order-time snapshot is a separate mechanism. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.thegamecrafter.com/developer/Game.html · keywords: Print order APIs and identical deck version control · also: https://help.thegamecrafter.com/article/429-how-to-order-your-game

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The Game Crafter counts only HTTP 200 as webhook success and retries failures. Its documentation says individual event retry status cannot be inspected; after 100 consecutive failures retries stop, and after 1000 consecutive failures the webhook deletes itself. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.thegamecrafter.com/developer/WebHook.html
- [statement] MakePlayingCards states that automated production queues the order after submission and that cancellations or changes cannot be made thereafter. Review the design and configuration before submitting, including when reordering. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.makeplayingcards.com/guarantee.aspx
- [statement] MPC documents reordering through a previous invoice/order, with changes to quantity, shipping and payment before submission and an Edit path for changing artwork. Its guarantee policy says cancellations and changes cannot be made after Submit Order. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.makeplayingcards.com/faq-order.aspx · keywords: Print order APIs and identical deck version control · also: https://www.makeplayingcards.com/guarantee.aspx

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The Game Crafter documents a cart workflow that creates a cart, attaches items, a destination, a shipping method and a user, then converts the cart to a receipt at payment; integrations can instead hand checkout to its website. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.thegamecrafter.com/developer/Cart.html
- [statement] The Game Crafter documents shop credit for private-label checkout; invoice payment and direct credit-card payment each require pre-approval. An API integration therefore needs an agreed payment route before automated ordering. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.thegamecrafter.com/developer/Cart.html
- [statement] The Game Crafter says each placed order snapshots the game contents and images. Later project edits do not alter that order; incorporating edits requires cancellation and a new order, and cancellation is unavailable once production starts. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-12-22) — https://help.thegamecrafter.com/article/429-how-to-order-your-game · keywords: Print order APIs and identical deck version control · also: https://help.thegamecrafter.com/article/110-will-my-order-include-changes-i-made-after-placing-the-order
- [statement] The Game Crafter exposes a Copy Game API method, which returns a game object. This provides a documented project-copy operation for maintaining separate revisions; the documentation does not establish a read-only release lock. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.thegamecrafter.com/developer/Game.html
- [statement] The Game Crafter documents sale, refund and shipment webhooks. The shipment event supplies a receipt with shipments included; the receiver can verify callback authenticity using the documented HMAC procedure. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.thegamecrafter.com/developer/WebHook.html
- [statement] MakePlayingCards documents reordering from an existing invoice/order, with options to change shipping, payment and quantity or edit the previous customized design in the cart before submission. A reorder is therefore an editable ordering workflow. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.makeplayingcards.com/faq-order.aspx
- [statement] DriveThruCards requires a physical proof before larger orders. For publication, the partner inspects the proof, corrects print files if needed, and activates the printed title only after accepting the proof. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23) — https://help.drivethrupartners.com/hc/en-us/articles/12780762858647-Card-Printing-The-Basics
- [statement] SignPath describes MPC Autofill as browser automation that downloads artwork and controls a test browser, and attributes this approach to MPC having no public API. This is an independent project description, not an MPC contractual API-support statement. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-09) — https://signpath.org/projects/mpc-autofill/
- [statement] Recommended release practice, inferred from the documented workflows: retain a separate approved artwork revision, preserve card sequence, record the proof decision and associate each submitted order with that revision. Do not use a mutable project name as the sole release record. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://help.thegamecrafter.com/article/429-how-to-order-your-game · keywords: Print order APIs and identical deck version control · also: https://www.makeplayingcards.com/faq-order.aspx, https://help.drivethrupartners.com/hc/en-us/articles/12780748203543-Specifications-for-Print-Cards, https://help.drivethrupartners.com/hc/en-us/articles/12780762858647-Card-Printing-The-Basics
- [statement] The Game Crafter describes edition as a version label and exposes update and copy operations. These are useful release-management primitives, but the cited Game documentation does not establish that an edition label makes artwork immutable. (low confidence) — https://www.thegamecrafter.com/developer/Game.html
- [statement] The Game Crafter webhook event list includes item sold, receipt refunded and receipt shipped. Shipment notification is therefore documented; that list does not establish a proof-approval or production-start callback. (low confidence) — https://www.thegamecrafter.com/developer/WebHook.html
- [statement] The Game Crafter documents signed webhook callbacks using SHA256 HMAC over epoch, a period and the unchanged JSON message, with the associated private key. (low confidence) — https://www.thegamecrafter.com/developer/WebHook.html
